newsitem.title: UK: Czech needs lower rates but FX is key-CNB official.
newsitem.headline: Czech needs lower rates but FX is key-CNB official.

text.p: The Czech economy needs interest rates to fall further but the Czech National Bank (CNB) is assessing the situation day by day to find an appropriate stance in line with a more stable exchange rates, a senior CNB official said Tuesday.

"The main task for the central bank is what to do with interest rates. We have to go down, it is necessary for the Czech economy, but there is a trade off between interest rates and the exchange rate," head of the CNB's Banking Supervision Josef Jilek told a conference in London.
Czech interest rates have eased from sky-high levels imposed to staunch the wave of adverse speculation against the crown last month but still remain more than double pre-crisis levels.
Today the CNB set an overnight repo tender to add liquidity to the market at a maximum rate of 31 percent. Its last repo tender to supply liquidity had an average yield of 72.37 percent on May 26.
Jilek declined to say what he saw as the appropriate level for the Czech crown but he said government plans to cut budget spending by about 30 billion crowns would help the situation.

"The next step is to lower the current account deficit and this will require the government to do some unpopular things," Jilek told the Risk Magazine conference on Central and East European currencies.
Private economists estimate the Czech Republic's current account deficit will balloon to as much as 10 percent of gross domestic product this year.

The CNB announced earlier on Tuesday that it agreed to lift informal limits on non-residents' access to the domestic Czech money market, a measure in place since the May currency crisis forced the central bank to abandon its currency peg and allow the crown to float more than 10 percent weaker.
